reading.finding: The two range-dependent positive constants are existential; neither is assigned a numerical value.

The notation declares that c and epsilon may denote different constants in different expressions. They depend on range and not volume. Treating successive c symbols as one evaluated number is invalid.
The smallness condition is qualitative. The text describes a contraction argument but does not display a numerical contraction radius for this star support.
The commutator estimate contains an unevaluated c; combinatorial estimates needed to extract it are not numerically reconstructed here.
The resolvent series assumes c times the local norm is less than one. This cannot yield a chosen numerical tau while c remains unevaluated.

Further proof details are attributed to Yarotsky, Perturbations of ground states in weakly interacting quantum spin systems, J. Math. Phys. 45, 2134-2152 (2004). That full paper's quantitative reconstruction was not completed in this loop.

conclusion: The reviewed primary source supports I1's qualitative application but this loop has not justified numerical constants for the three-dimensional star with infinite-dimensional rotor sites.
